This year marks a period of generational disruption. With global aid projected to decline by up to 22% this year, the Global South faces mounting pressure to chart its own energy future. However, at the same time, South-South trade has now surpassed North-South trade, making up 28% of global exchange.

A shift is already underway: BRICS is expanding, South Africa is chairing the G20, and across regions, the Global South is asserting new agency to shape its energy future on its own terms.

📢 Read the latest Sustainable Energy Bulletin which highlights opportunities driving South-South leadership in energy transitions: 👉 https://lnkd.in/ecsVJf4T

As the Sevilla Commitment is adopted at #FfD4 - aiming to reform the international financial architecture, reduce borrowing costs and close the sustainable development financing gap - four priorities in regional and South-South cooperation stand out:

1️⃣ Expand regional trade and investment ecosystems, such as the African Continental Free Trade Area which is projected to increase FDI in energy infrastructure by 111% to 159%

2️⃣ Accelerate regional exchange and value chains, such as integrated power markets that can drive shared prosperity.

3️⃣ Leverage AI and digital tools to power innovation rooted in place - geographically, linguistically & culturally.

4️⃣ Mobilize catalytic finance through South-South and triangular cooperation

At stake is energy justice. 666 million people still lack electricity, and 1.18 billion live in energy poverty. What role do you see for South-South and regional partnerships in shaping the future of energy transitions? Share your thoughts below👇
